sentences: Ordering food for guests could soon become more convenient on Zomato.
The food delivery app is getting ready to launch a new feature called Mehmaan Mode, aimed at allowing consumers to pick dishes without having to view their prices.
The concept is to simplify ordering meals for other people, particularly if they are hosting guests and want to pay for everyone.
The suggestion was made on the social network LinkedIn, where Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal confirmed the imminent launch.
The feature will be rolled out this week, Goyal said.
The company doesn't, however, have released all of the specifics surrounding how it works or its accessibility.
The proposed feature addresses an important issue that is faced by most households in India.
When guests arrive at home, people usually give their smartphones to friends and family and ask them to select the food they want to have.
This can be easy for them to order, but it can also make them feel uneasy about ordering the more expensive food items when someone else is paying.
People will put their searching minds at ease with the aid of Mehmaan Mode, because this feature conceals prices while they browse the food options available.
Guests could view the menu and make their selections without worrying about the price of what they are ordering.
The host would continue to be liable for the final bill.
After all of the selections have been made, the person ordering it may be able to review the selections and finalize the deal.
This feature might be useful at festivals, and at family gatherings and other events where a number of people come home together.
It can also help hosts who wish to provide their guests with options to make choices based on their preferences.
But, these are the intended benefits of the proposed feature.
The final design and whether all the proposed functions will be available in the launch have not yet been confirmed by Zomato.
Itu Chaudhuri Design's Marketing Manager Ayushmaan Agarwalla had the idea.
He mentioned in a LinkedIn post the need of Zomato to have a special mode when ordering food together.
Sharing the phones to make a group order is a common practice, said Agarwalla.
His proposal is a special feature that hides prices temporarily, which would make it easier for guests and hosts.
The idea was to address a social issue rather than a technical problem with food delivery, and the social issue was one that most people could easily recognise.
The guests would not need to be concerned with the cost of their selections, and hosts would be able to choose freely.
Goyal directly responded to the post and accepted the recommendation.
Zomato will be rolling out the feature this week, he said, hinting that the company has intentions of proceeding with the idea.
His reply got responses on LinkedIn, which put this proposed feature in the spotlight.
However, the exchange didn't confirm if it would be available to all users at once or phased in.
There are several points that aren't clear about Mehmaan Mode.
Zomato hasn't specified what users will have to do to enable it.
It's not known, either, if the feature will obscure prices for the entire menu or at a specific stage in the ordering process.
The company has not yet disclosed if guests will be able to add items directly to the cart, if the host will have any control over what is in the cart or if there will be any limitations.
These will inform the usefulness of the feature in the real world.
It might be more convenient for households that often place orders for meals for large groups if the process was simple to activate and there was an easy way to view the final order.
There's no official announcement yet on how this feature will work in practice; in the meantime, users will have to wait for such an announcement.
Mehmaan Mode will provide an additional choice to Zomato's ordering process, if it is successful.
The feature is not about changing the way food is being delivered, but rather about making it easier for the "host" to select a meal when he is the one taking care of others.
